- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days), suggesting a persistent upward bias.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or too high after sharp price spikes in history, indicating overshoot behavior.
- Model underestimates late-period price movements (last 5–10 days) relative to true outcomes, suggesting mean reversion or lag in capturing sustained trends.
- Forecasts show a tendency to “smooth” volatility — underreacting to sudden drops or overreacting to minor rises — implying poor sensitivity to short-term market shocks.
- Model often fails to capture the “tail” of price increases (e.g., final 5–10 days of forecast vs. true outcome), suggesting horizon-specific underestimation of upward momentum.
- When history includes a strong upward trend, model tends to overreact with a sharp peak, then overcorrects — indicating a lag in adjusting to sustained momentum.
- Model exhibits a “memory decay” effect — recent history (last 5–10 days) is underweighted in forecasting, leading to underestimation of true price evolution.
